title: Structured rulebook + automated scorer for enterprise IAM/admin requests
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers submit a wide range of admin and IAM requests (RBAC role changes, SSO/SAML setups, SCIM provisioning, org policy exceptions). Current intake is manual, inconsistent across tiers, and hard to prioritize. We need a reproducible, auditable decision surface that classifies requests, assigns a priority score, and automates low-risk flows to meet SLAs while containing security risk.

Goal: Deliver a structured rulebook (taxonomy + deterministic heuristics) combined with an automated priority scorer (weighted signals) integrated into the intake form and routing pipeline so that: (1) trivial requests can be actioned faster or auto-approved with audit trail; (2) high-risk/compliance requests are flagged for senior review; (3) PM/Eng/Support capacity is allocated predictably using objective scores.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form updated to capture canonical fields for IAM: request_type, org_size, contract_tier, impacted_resources, data_sensitivity, requested_timeline, justification, SSO_provider, SCIM_scope.
Rulebook defined with at least 12 explicit rules mapping request patterns to 'risk' (low/medium/high) and 'default SLA' (24h/3d/7d).
Automated scorer implemented server-side producing a numeric priority 0-100 and categorical label (low/medium/high) for each submission.
Integration: score and label written to ticket payload and visible in Console intake queue UI column.
Safety: auto-approve flow exists for low-risk requests and requires cryptographic audit log entry and optional 24h rollback window.
Telemetry: measureable metrics (TTR median, percent auto-approved, override rate) emitted to Console dashboards.
Security review completed and signed-off by InfoSec before alpha rollout.
Pilot run with 5 enterprise customers showing 30% reduction in manual triage time and <=5% false-auto-approve overrides.
proposed_solution: Phase 1: Build a canonical intake schema and static rulebook (taxonomic mapping of request types + deterministic guards). Phase 2: Implement a weighted scorer combining deterministic rules and simple heuristics (org_size_weight, contract_weight, data_sensitivity_weight, prior_support_activity_weight). Phase 3: Wire scoring into intake pipeline, show in Console queue, and add feature-flagged auto-approve paths with audit logging. Phase 4: Collect feedback and telemetry; iterate toward ML-assisted ranking if needed.
tradeoffs: Auto-approval reduces latency but increases risk — will require conservative whitelist and post-approval audits.
Heavy rulebook coverage increases upfront PM/Eng effort and maintenance cost as new request types appear.
A pure ML model improves ranking but is opaque; starting with deterministic rules ensures auditable decisions.
Adding more fields to intake reduces ambiguity but increases friction for customers — balance by progressive disclosure (minimal required fields + optional advanced form).
rollout_plan: Week 0-2: Finalize canonical schema and rulebook with Security/Support/Eng/DS input; create PRD and acceptance tests.
Week 3-4: Engineering builds intake schema, scoring service (feature-flagged), and Console UI column; Design provides microcopy and form UX.
Week 5: Internal alpha with Support and 2 trusted pilot customers; monitor audit logs and override workflows.
Week 6-8: Expand pilot to 5 customers, enable conservative auto-approve for a subset of low-risk request types; run daily review of auto-approved items.
Week 9: Security sign-off and gradual ramp to auto-processing for additional request types; bake into console-2025.04 release.
Fallbacks: ability to disable auto-approve per-customer and immediate manual revert flow for mistaken approvals.
metrics: Median Time To Resolution (all IAM requests)
Percent of tickets re-opened due to misclassification
Support/Eng triage hours saved per week
notes: Potential data source: existing support logs + org meta from billing/entitlements service to seed weights.
Cross-team owners: Support (triage), Security (policy), Infra (audit logs), Eng (scoring service), Design (form UX).
